ventures.title: Volatility-Adjusted Position-Sizing Spreadsheet for Retail Traders
ventures.thesis: Retail crypto/FX/equity traders routinely blow up accounts by sizing positions off gut feel instead of volatility. A ready-to-use spreadsheet that auto-computes position size from account equity, risk-per-trade %, and ATR-based stop distance is a proven, evergreen digital-product category (similar templates sell steadily on Gumroad/Etsy for $9-$29). Zero marginal cost, legal, no impersonation, pure genuine utility — I can fully draft the logic and layout now; a human just needs to build it in Sheets/Excel and list it.
ventures.deliverable:
SPREADSHEET SPEC + FORMULAS (ready to build in Google Sheets/Excel):

TAB 1: 'RiskCalc'
Columns: A=Asset, B=Account Equity ($), C=Risk % per trade (default 1%), D=Entry Price, E=Stop Price, F=Stop Distance = ABS(D-E), G=Risk $ = B*C, H=Position Size (units) = G/F, I=Position Notional ($) = H*D, J=Max Leverage Check = I/B (flag red if >5x via conditional formatting).

TAB 2: 'ATR Helper' — instructions for pulling 14-period ATR from TradingView/exchange and using ATR*multiplier (1.5-2x) as stop distance instead of a manual guess, with a worked example (BTC entry $86,000, ATR $1,800, stop = entry - 1.5*ATR = $83,300, on $10k account risking 1%, size = $100/$2,700 = 0.037 BTC = $3,182 notional).

TAB 3: 'Portfolio Heat' — sums risk $ across all open positions (pulls from Tab1 col G), flags if total open risk exceeds 6% of equity (conditional format red), enforcing a hard portfolio-level stop-loss discipline.

TAB 4: 'Trade Log' — Date, Asset, Direction, Entry, Exit, R-multiple realized (=(
 Exit-Entry)/Stop Distance), running equity curve chart.

Include a 1-page README explaining the 1%-risk rule, why volatility-based stops beat fixed %, and how to adapt multiplier by asset class (crypto 2x ATR, FX 1.5x ATR, equities 2x ATR).

ventures.title: Crypto DCA & Rebalance Planner (Google Sheets Template)
ventures.thesis: Retail crypto holders constantly ask 'how much should I buy/sell to get back to target weights' but don't want to build a spreadsheet. A clean, pre-built Google Sheets template that (a) tracks a target allocation across BTC/ETH/alts/stables, (b) computes drift vs targets, and (c) outputs exact buy/sell $ amounts to rebalance or to execute a scheduled DCA — sold once on Gumroad/Etsy for $9-15, zero marginal cost per sale, pure content/skill monetization, no ToS issues, no financial advice given (just arithmetic on user-entered numbers).
ventures.deliverable:
SHEET STRUCTURE (ready to build in Google Sheets, tabs and formulas specified):

TAB 1 'Setup': Columns A=Asset, B=Target Weight %, C=Current Holdings (units), D=Current Price (user pastes), E=Current Value =C*D, F=Total Portfolio Value =SUM(E), G=Current Weight % =E/F, H=Target Value =B*F, I=Drift $ =H-E, J=Action ('BUY'/'SELL'/'HOLD' via =IF(I>1,"BUY",IF(I<-1,"SELL","HOLD")), K=Amount to Trade $ =ABS(I).
Rows pre-filled for BTC, ETH, SOL, Stablecoin, 'Alts basket' — user edits freely, adds rows.

TAB 2 'DCA Schedule': Columns for Date, Planned Contribution $, Split % per asset (defaults to Target Weight from Tab1 via QUERY/VLOOKUP), computed $ per asset, running total invested, running total units bought (=Contribution*Split/Price entered that date) — gives a full DCA log the user fills in weekly/monthly.

TAB 3 'Dashboard': Pie chart of current vs target weights (native Sheets chart on Tab1 ranges), a single-cell total drift metric =SUMPRODUCT(ABS(I2:I10)) to show 'how far out of balance am I', and conditional formatting (red/green) on the Action column.

TAB 4 'Read Me': Plain-English instructions (no advice, just mechanics): how to fill in prices, how often to rebalance (e.g. monthly or >5% drift), disclaimer that this is a calculator not financial advice.

All formulas above are copy-paste-ready native Google Sheets syntax — this is a fully specified, buildable template, not just a concept.
